definition: A generative framework that learns a direct continuous transport from noise to data, simplifying diffusion training and enabling high quality in very few sampling steps.
details: A generative framework that learns a direct continuous transport from noise to data, simplifying diffusion training and enabling high quality in very few sampling steps. Rapidly adopted in image (SD3, Flux) and speech synthesis.

explainer.lead: Flow matching is a way to train generative systems to turn random noise into images, speech, or other data by learning a continuous path between them. Its simpler training approach and ability to produce high-quality results in few sampling steps have made it useful in systems such as SD3 and Flux.

tiers.eli5: Imagine slowly reshaping a cloud of random scribbles until it becomes a picture. Flow matching teaches a computer which way to push the scribbles at every moment, rather than making it guess the finished picture all at once. Following those pushes can create a good result with only a few moves.
tiers.practitioner: Train a model to predict the time-dependent velocity along continuous paths from noise to data, then generate by integrating that learned field from a noise sample. It is applied in image generation systems including SD3 and Flux, as well as speech synthesis. Few-step sampling still depends on accurate integration; flow matching does not automatically make generation one-step.
tiers.paperLevel: Flow matching learns a vector field v_theta(t,x) such that dx/dt = v_theta(t,x), with x(0) sampled from noise and x(1) intended to follow the data distribution. Training fits this field along continuous noise-to-data paths, simplifying diffusion-style training; sampling still requires numerical integration, even when only a few steps are used.

explainer.example: To generate an image, the system starts with random noise at time 0. Its learned field indicates how to update the noisy state at successive times, and a numerical solver follows those updates until time 1, producing the final image in only a few steps.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating generation as a long sequence of separate corrections, flow matching learns the direction and speed needed to move smoothly from noise toward realistic data. A new sample is made by starting with noise and following that learned motion through time.
howItWorks: Pair noise with training data along continuous paths.
Learn the velocity that moves samples along those paths.
At generation time, begin with a fresh noise sample.
Integrate the learned velocity field to reach a data sample.
Use few integration steps when high-quality fast sampling is needed.
explainer.whyItMatters: Flow matching simplifies diffusion training while supporting high-quality generation with very few sampling steps. That combination helps explain its rapid adoption in image and speech generation.
misconceptions: Flow matching is a training and generation framework, not a specific image model.
Few-step sampling does not necessarily mean one-step sampling or eliminate numerical integration.
